title: Session store migration: tradeoffs of A, B and C

blocks.title: Every option has an open condition before the Q4 peak

blocks.markdown: The session store has to leave the single Postgres primary before the Q4 peak, 9 weeks out. As written, no option clears every constraint: A and C need downtime Product has not approved, and B depends on an unfixed bug and a driver release with no date. The points below are numbered so you can comment on each one. Line references (L7, L22) point to DECISION.md; *inference* marks reasoning that goes beyond the doc.

columns.title: A: in-place schema migration
columns.markdown:
**A1. Downtime.** 40 min planned window (L7). Product has approved no customer-visible downtime (L22), so A needs that approval or proof the window is invisible to customers.

**A2. Does it meet the goal?** Line 3 says the store must move *off the single Postgres primary*. An "in-place" migration does not say how that happens. Worth confirming before anything else. *(inference)*

**A3. The window is the risk.** Data-loss is "low if the window holds" (L9). Both outages last year came from long-running migrations (L16), which is exactly how a window fails to hold. That history is about availability, not proven data loss. *(inference)*

**A4. Rollback is lossy.** Snapshot restore loses writes made since the window opened (L8). The later you decide to roll back, the more you lose.

**A5. Most schedule margin.** 2 weeks, 1 engineer, no dependency (L10, L11): about 7 weeks of margin before peak (L18). *(inference)*

**A6. Cheapest.** About 2 engineer-weeks if full time. *(inference)*

columns.title: B: dual-write with backfill
columns.markdown:
**B1. Downtime.** None planned (L7). The only option that meets the downtime constraint as written. Planned zero is not proof of zero customer impact. *(inference)*

**B2. Known correctness bug.** The backfill race produced 0.3% mismatches in staging and is understood but not fixed (L9, L17). Unknown: 0.3% of what, and whether mismatches can be detected and repaired before reads switch over.

**B3. Cleanest rollback.** Stop dual-write and read the old store (L8). The only rollback with no stated loss, provided the old store stays complete and authoritative the whole time. *(inference)*

**B4. External dependency.** Needs driver 4.2, release date unconfirmed (L11). Part of the schedule is outside the team's control.

**B5. Schedule.** 5 weeks, 2 engineers (L10): about 4 weeks of margin, but only if the driver is ready when work starts. *(inference)*

**B6. Load during migration.** Backfill and dual-write add work to a primary with about 12.5% headroom at forecast peak (L15), so finishing well before peak matters. *(inference)*

**B7. Cost.** About 10 engineer-weeks. *(inference)*

columns.title: C: new service with cutover
columns.markdown:
**C1. Downtime.** 5 min cutover (L7). Shorter than A, but still needs product approval if customers can see it (L22).

**C2. No schedule buffer.** 8 weeks, 3 engineers (L10), finishing one week before peak "with no slack" (L18). Any slip pushes cutover or stabilisation into the peak. The doc does not say whether that last week is already reserved. *(inference)*

**C3. Rollback is lossy.** DNS revert loses every session created after cutover (L8). The "low" data-loss rating (L9) describes the forward path, not rollback. DNS propagation time is not addressed. *(inference)*

**C4. New operational load.** Needs a new on-call rotation (L11). A new service goes live just before peak with a rotation that does not exist yet; its readiness date is not stated.

**C5. Most expensive.** About 24 engineer-weeks (L10). Whether three engineers are free now is not stated. *(inference)*

items: **X1. Capacity margin is thin, not zero.** The primary saturates at 1.8x today's peak; forecast is 1.6x (L15). A forecast error of 12.5% reaches saturation. Doing nothing survives the forecast on paper, which is why a migration that slips *into* the peak can be worse than one that never started. *(inference)*

**X2. The data-loss row compares different things.** A's rating is conditional on the window, B's is an observed staging defect, C's covers only the forward path. Read rollback loss (L8) separately from forward-path risk (L9).

**X3. Each option is blocked by a different owner.** A and C wait on a Product decision about downtime (L22). B waits on engineering (the race fix) and an outside release (driver 4.2). Who can clear their blocker this week may matter as much as the table.
**X4. No option states its end state.** Only line 3 states the goal. For each option, ask for the target architecture and the point where the single primary stops mattering.
**X5. Estimates are point values.** No ranges, no staffing confirmation, no statement of whether they include validation and rollback rehearsal (L10).
